03

WCAG Site Audit

Is your site accessible — or does it quietly fail the visitors who arrive with a keyboard, a screen reader, or a magnifier? Most owners have never checked. Their customers check every day, and the answer decides real sales. I audit your site against WCAG and hand you a well-written report you can actually understand: every failure explained in plain English, never spec jargon.

Qualified business owners can order the full recode report: every failure paired with its documented fix, ready to hand to any web development studio to carry out. I audit and document; the building is theirs. Curious where your site stands? Take a first taste of the audit right here:

NEW · INTERACTIVE · ABOUT 2–3 MINUTES

The accessibility self-check

Fifteen short questions about the barriers your visitors actually hit — each with a tiny live demo, so you feel the problem instead of reading a paragraph about it. Answer honestly: yes, not sure, or no. At the end you get graded like school — A+ through F — plus the broad areas behind the grade, and the option to have a slightly expanded version of the report emailed to you.

  • 15 QUESTIONS
  • NO CODE NEEDED
  • KEYBOARD · SCREEN READERS · VOICE · ZOOM · SWITCHES · BRAILLE · AI AIDS
QUESTION 1 OF 15

Your results
–

Broad areas behind your grade

This report stays broad on purpose — it’s built from your answers alone, and nobody has audited your site yet. The specifics live in the audit.

    Why this is a business question, not a nicety: WCAG 2.1 AA is the yardstick courts and regulators actually measure against — ADA Title III in the US, Section 508 for anyone selling to government, the European Accessibility Act for products sold into the EU. And the failures behind most claims, failed bids, and lost contracts are rarely exotic. They’re a short list of basics — the same list this self-check just walked you through. Fixing them needs no exotic technology either: semantic markup, real names and labels, measured contrast, and testing with the tools your customers actually use — JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, a keyboard alone, a 400% zoom.

    That’s the audit Circuit Research runs: your live site, tested against the WCAG success criteria with the tools your customers use. The deliverable is the recode report — every failure documented with the fix it needs, in plain English — ready to hand to any web development studio to carry out. Ask about the audit.

    Get the expanded version of this report by email

    Want the fuller picture? Trade your email for a slightly more expanded version of your self-check report: the same broad areas, opened up a step further, with your letter grade explained in full — still based on your answers, since your site hasn’t been audited yet. That same email carries the option to order the full recode report: the complete audit document, every failure with its fix documented, ready to take to any web development studio. The full report is a paid document, offered to qualified business owners.

    // SIGNALS FROM THE FEED

    Recent research, by the numbers

    Skeptical? Good — don’t take my word for any of this. The feed is the portfolio: every post a real piece of research, written in plain English, published where anyone can read it, check it, and argue with it — long before you’d ever hire anyone. Here’s what the latest run turned up:

    $891B

    Stablecoin transfer volume in Q3 — on a flat supply of roughly $301B.

    Same pile of money, moving much faster. Velocity — not issuance — is the story of the quarter.

    SOURCE: Q3 STABLECOIN DATA, REPORTED OCT 2026
    459,653,000

    The slot where Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade went live.

    A consensus overhaul years in the making — and the research caught the exact slot it switched on.

    SOURCE: SOLANA NETWORK DATA, OCT 2026
    16

    Issuers formally objecting to tokenized-stock listings under the SEC Innovation Exemption.

    Tokenization is coming. The incumbents just intend it to arrive on their terms.

    SOURCE: SEC FILING COVERAGE, OCT 2026
    90%+

    Of Web3 games have failed — 300+ shut down, studio funding down 93%.

    And yet gaming remains the only dapp category still growing, at roughly 4.9M daily wallets. Play-to-earn died. Playing didn’t.

    SOURCES: COINDESK · DAPPRADAR, 2026
    // HOW IT WORKS

    The method, and the person running it

    Four habits, one founder — no account managers, no handoffs, no game of telephone between you and the work.

    Clear from the first line

    If the first line doesn’t earn the second, nothing else matters. Every piece opens with the most interesting true thing in it — stated plainly, so it’s understood at a glance.

    Sources cited, caveats named

    Every claim traces to a source you can check, and the honest limits of the data get said out loud — a wallet is not a player.

    Ends with a question

    Research should start conversations, not close them. Most pieces close by asking the reader the thing the data can’t answer.

    Built to be read by everyone

    The accessibility work and the writing work are the same work: structure, clarity, and respect for the person on the other end.
